title: Chapter 290: Coffin Village
html:
The spiderweb had formed a line of words. Strangely, the moment Master Bai looked toward them, they dissolved into blood and washed away in the rain.

“You’ve been searching for Jiang Ling’s sister’s body; is it because you’ve done some wrong by her?” Chen Ge heard the guilt and self-reprimand in the old man’s words.

“Come inside.” Master Bai hung the lamp beside the door, visibly shaken that a secret kept for years had been exposed. Chen Ge followed him into the second hut. The old man released a long sigh. “I believe I know who poisoned the couple.”

“You do?” Chen Ge stood at the door holding the hammer; he did not walk in.

“I have a theory.” Master Bai shifted the wooden bed, revealing a small, pitch-black coffin hidden beneath it.

“Placing a coffin under the bed?” Chen Ge was confused.

“I prepared it for the Zhu family’s elder daughter.” The old man opened the lid and removed an unfinished memorial tablet carved with the name Zhu Xinrou.

“Why did you prepare this coffin for her? Are you related to her disappearance?”

“The story began long ago.” Master Bai stared blankly at the tablet. “When I was a child, adults spoke of a place called Coffin Village deep in the Jiujiang mountains. Its inhabitants never mingled with outsiders, and many bore strange deformities. They also observed unsettling customs, such as keeping a coffin for a living person in every home. No one knew why.”

The first part made sense to Chen Ge. Isolation would have encouraged marriage among close relatives, increasing the likelihood of congenital deformities. The rest, however, baffled him.

What is the meaning behind every family owning a living coffin? Placing a coffin inside the house is much too unlucky.

Chen Ge closed the door and softly asked, “Master Bai, is the village still there today?”

“At first I assumed the village was only a legend. No one I knew had ever seen it. Then, one day, we learned the truth.” Master Bai set down the tablet and searched inside the coffin. “About a decade ago, disaster struck Coffin Village, and several families escaped.

“The refugees appeared perfectly normal and did not practice any of the rumored customs, so Bai Family Village at the foot of the mountain accepted them. No one expected an epidemic to strike our village that same year.” Regret saturated Master Bai’s voice. Some residents had apparently opposed admitting the refugees, but the majority welcomed them.

“The few families brought the epidemic out from inside the mountains?”

“Who can say? Anyone able to leave eventually moved away, and the village became nearly deserted. The families from Coffin Village remained, however, and put down roots. Later, they even changed its name. That settlement is the Lin Guan Village you saw tonight.” Master Bai finally found what he sought: a black garment.

“This was made for the Zhu family’s elder daughter. People who died away from home were dressed in black before being placed in their coffins, so the blood would be less visible.”

The garment possessed one disturbing feature: four short sleeves, each about a quarter of normal length, had been sewn into its back.

“You see how strange it is, don’t you? But this garment was cut to fit the Zhu family’s elder daughter.” Master Bai’s voice diminished until it was barely audible, laden with pain. “Her parents were among those who escaped Coffin Village. Her mother was already carrying her when they fled, which made the child the village’s final ‘seed.’”

“A deformity this extreme cannot be explained by close-relative marriage alone. Something is deeply wrong with Coffin Village.”

Chen Ge did not expect that would be the answer. Looking at the black jacket, Chen Ge could imagine what Zhu Xinrou looked like.

“I know little about what afflicted Coffin Village. I only know the child lived miserably. Her parents feared anyone seeing her, so even in scorching weather they wrapped her in layer after layer of clothing.

“As she grew older, concealing her became impossible. Her parents eventually locked her inside the house to prevent her from leaving.”

The old man folded the outfit and placed it on the coffin lid. It would serve its purpose soon.

“Then, what happened?”

“Eventually, the villagers discovered the Zhu family’s elder daughter. To my astonishment, the other families from Coffin Village did not defend her parents. They wanted the poor child killed.

“The dispute nearly became a riot. In the end, the original residents of Bai Family Village calmed the crowd and expelled the Zhu family. The father was a coffin maker and skilled carpenter. After leaving, he moved his family to this peach orchard, where they lived in isolation.

“Life went on as usual, and there was a rumor in the village that the family had given birth to a second daughter.

“Just when everyone believed we had heard the last of them, the couple rushed back to warn the village that their elder daughter had disappeared. You heard correctly: they did not ask us to help find her. They warned us to be careful.

“Several days later, they found her in the mountains and dragged her home for punishment. They suspended her with ropes and beat her.

“She escaped every few months. Each time they found her, they dragged her back and punished her brutally.

“The wooden hut that was built at the deepest part of the plantation was used to lock up the eldest daughter. To punish her, her father even built a special device.

“The villagers treated the elder daughter as a monster, while her parents appeared to regret her birth. Only her little sister showed her kindness and regarded her as family.

“The younger daughter also had an abnormality, though nothing as visible as her sister’s. She was sweet and adorable, and everyone loved her.” Master Bai sighed. “My land bordered the orchard, so I often met the little girl. She was never shy around strangers, and we quickly became friends.

“One day, while I worked in my field, she came to me in tears and begged me to save her sister. I knew what her family was like, yet I ignored her…”

Master Bai’s voice broke. His clouded eyes remained fixed on the black garment as his hands gripped his knees. “I should have helped, no matter what people called her. The girl left in tears. Eventually my worry overcame my fear, and I came to the orchard to investigate.

“I found the elder daughter inside the fourth hut. That was the last time I ever saw her alive. Her body was shackled to the wooden frame, every arm bound with rope. Wounds covered her, and she seemed close to death.

“I couldn’t imagine what she had endured. She begged me to save her, but terror overcame me, and I fled.

“Several days later, I finally gathered enough courage to return, but the couple told me that their eldest daughter had escaped again.”
